 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition U/s 166 of the Motor vehicles Act 1989, claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% from date of accident till Saroja.

K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132534733/
1 date of realization, in respect of death of Sri.PrasadaK.S. who succumbed to injuries on 10.03.2023 in Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief facts of the petitioner are summarized as under:
On 10.03.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., the deceased Prasada.K.S. was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EF-1978 from Magadi to Jalamanagala Main Road, near Krishnanjineya Temple, Kottgarahalli, Madabal Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagara, Karnataka.
At that time, the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F- 2076 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries on all over the body.
3. Immediately after the accident the deceased was shifted to Government Hospital wherein post mortem was conducted.
On examination, doctor has opined that, the deceased was succumbed to injuries on his way to the hospital.
The petitioners have incurred huge amount towards transportation, funeral and other expenses.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased Prasada.K.S. was very hale and healthy and he was an agriculturist and self employed.
He was earning Rs.25,000/- per month from said avocation and he used to contribute all his earnings towards maintenance of his family.
Due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony and their lives have come to stand still.
The petitioner No.1 is wife of the deceased and petitioner No.2 is the mother of deceased and they have lost love and affection of the deceased and their lives have become miserable.
5. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent drive of the respondent, who drove his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-2076.
The respondent is the owner of the vehicle involved in the accident and accident has taken place due to the negligent drive of the offender bus driver.
Hence the respondent is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore the petitioner prays to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest at 18% p.a., from the date of accident till the realization.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
6. After registration of the petition, notice was issued against respondent.
In pursuance of service of notice the respondent has appeared through its counsel and has filed its written statement on behalf of respondent by denying the entire petition averments.
The respondent further pleaded that the deceased was not possessing valid driving license on the date of accident.
Further denied the expenses incurred for funeral ceremony.
Further denied the age of the deceased, avocation and income of the said deceased.
Further denied the other contents of the petition.
The compensation has claimed by the petitioners are highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
Saroja.

In order to substantiate the claim petition, the 1 st petitioner is examined as PW.1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.
The respondent has examined its driver as RW.1 and no documents marked on its behalf.
8. I have heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials available on record.

9. Upon considering rival contentions raised by the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
1. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Prasada.K.S. died in the Motor vehicle accident that occurred on 10.03.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., on Magadi-Jalamangala Road, near Krishnanjaneya Temple, Kottagarahalli, Madabal Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramangara due to the rash and negligence driving of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 42-F-2076 by its driver?
2.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for the compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
4 . What order or award?
10. My findings on the above issues are as under.
Issue No.1:

In the affirmative,
 Issue No.2: In the affirmative.
 Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per the final orders for

the following:-
 REASONS  ISSUE NO.1:
11.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 10.03.2023 at about 5.00 p.m., the deceased Prasada.K.S. was proceeding in motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EF-1978 from Magadi to Jalamanagala Main Road, near Krishnanjineya Temple, Kottgarahalli, Madabal Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara, Karnataka.
At that time, the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F- 2076 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
Due to the impact of accident, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries on all over the body.
12. To substantiate the petition averments, petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 10 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10.
Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 FIR and complaint which reveals Saroja.K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132534733/
3 that one Nagendra Prasada.K.P has lodged complaint on 10.03.2023 against the driver of the respondent offender vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-2076.

Upon the complaint,
the police have registered FIR for the offence punishable under section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.
The Ex.P.6 is the Inquest report which clearly discloses that, Prasada.K.S has died on 10.03.2023 in a Road Traffic Accident.
Ex.P.3 and 4 are the spot mahazar along with sketch which speaks about the occurrence of accident.
Ex.P.5 is the PM report which reveals that, deceased has succumbed to the injuries in the said accident.
Ex.P.9 is the IMV report.

Ex.P.10 is the charge sheet which reveals that,
police have investigated the matter and filed charge sheet against the driver of the offender vehicle i.e., KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F- 2076.
13.
The Respondent has examined its driver as RW.1 by name Dasthagir Sabdada.
The said RW.1 has deposed that he is working as KSRTC bus driver and conversant with the facts of this case.
On 10.03.2023 he was in duty at KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F2026 in the schedule trip from Ramanagar to Magadi.
He was proceeding slowly and cautiously by observing all traffic rules in peak traffic hours.

While so proceeding near Krishnanjineya Temple, Kottgarahalli, Madabal Hobli,
Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara the deceased person being a rider of TVS Wega motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-41-EF- 1978 came in high speed and dashed his bus.
The deceased person had fell down from his vehicle and got accident for himself.
The alleged accident has occurred due to the sole contributory negligent act of the deceased person.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
14. RW.1 was subjected to cross-examination by learned counsel for the petitioner.
During the course of cross-examination RW.1 has admitted that the police have filed charge sheet against him for the alleged accident.
He has not furnished any document to show that he has challenged the charge sheet stating that the accident was not occurred by his fault.
15. Per contra, the evidence of PW.1 clearly reveals that the accident has took place by the fault of the offender vehicle driver i.e., RW.1.
During the course of further cross-examination of PW.1 nothing was elicited from the mouth of PW.1, so as to disbelieve his version.
Hence, this court is of the view that the petitioner has proved that due to the rash and negligent driver of the KSRTC driver the accident has took place on the day of accident.

16. Therefore, it is apparent on the face of records that, the respondent has admitted the occurrence of accident and death of deceased has caused due to the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-2076.
In the absence of any cogent materials from the respondents in this regard.
The only inference which has to be drawn is that, the accident in question was the result of the rash and negligent drive of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-F-2076.
Hence, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
ISSUE NO.2 17.
The PW.1 in her evidence has deposed that, her deceased husband Prasada K.S. was agriculturist and self employed and was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Her husband was aged about 58 years and was hale and healthy before the occurrence of accident.
Petitioners being wife and mother of the deceased Prasada.K.S. were wholly dependent on the income of the said deceased, he being a sole Saroja.

4 bread earning member in his family.
She has further deposed that, he has spent huge amount towards funeral and other expenses.

18. Petitioners have averred in the petition that, the petitioner No.1 is the wife of the deceased,
Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
To substantiate the same, PW.1 has produced notarized copies of Aadhar cards along with originals of herself and petitioner No.2.
These documents reflects the relationship of deceased with the petitioners.
The oral and documentary evidence led by PW.1 reflects that, petitioners are the LR's of deceased Prasada K.S.,.
Since, the respondent has not contested the said matter in the evidence led by PW.1.
Then the evidence of PW.1 stands unshaken and the same is sufficient to show that petitioners are the LR's of deceased.

Accordingly, I answer issue No.2 In the affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
19.

Basically three facts lead to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death as per Sarla Verma Case i.e., (i) age of deceased,
(ii) Income of deceased and (iii) Number of dependents.
(i) Age of deceased:
According to the petitioners the age of the deceased at the time of the accident was 58 years.
As per the aadhar card marked at Ex.P.11, wherein the date of the birth of the deceased mentioned as 08.05.1965, the accident was occurred on 10.03.2023.
So, as on the date of the accident the deceased was aged 58 years.
(ii).Income of the deceased: According to the petitioners deceased Prasada.K.S. was agriculturist and self employed and he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any documents.
Under the circumstances, this court has to consider the notional income to assess the loss of dependency.

20. In Legal Manager IFFCO Tokio GIC Ltd., V/s Srinivasa and Others, 2018 SCC online Kar 2862 Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "the court cannot ignore the notional income chart of the Lokadalath when there is no material evidence to prove the actual income.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Hence, in the absence of material on record to prove the actual income of the deceased as on the date of occurrence of accident, the charge formulated by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru is to be followed to asses the notional income of deceased as on the date of accident".
21.

entities.text: Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru while holding Lokadalath, has determined the notional income at Rs.16,000/- if the accident had occurred in the year-2023 and thus income of the deceased Prasada.K.S. is to be considered at Rs.16,000/- per month.
22. Loss of dependency:

The following issues are to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at loss of dependency, they are (i) addition/deduction to be made for arriving at the income.
Saroja.

K vs K.S.R.T.C on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132534733/
5
(ii) Deductions to be made towards the personal living expenses of the deceased.
(iii) The multiplier to be applied with reference to the age of the deceased.

23. As per the decision reported in National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that "if the deceased is below 40 years 40% of the established income of deceased towards future prospectus; an addition of 25%
where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years; an addition 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as necessary method of computation."

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Other reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the same formula to the case on hand it is clear that, the deceased is entitled for future prospects.
In the present case the deceased is aged between 50 to 60 years and therefore 10% of the established income of the deceased is assessed towards future prospects.
Hence, the future prospects is determined as Rs.1,600/- (16,000 X 10/100 = Rs.1,600/-).
Therefore the total income of the deceased is determined as Rs.17,600/- per month (16,000 + 1,600 = Rs.17,600/-).
24. Admittedly, petitioner No.1 and 2 are the dependents of deceased person.

As per the the Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298 case, when there are 2 or 3 Dependents 1/3rd of the income is to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased.

entities.text: Sarla Verma V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and others reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As such 1/3rd amount is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses i.e.,
Rs.5,867/-.
When the said 1/3rd amount is deducted from monthly income of the deceased, then the balance amount shall be Rs.11,733/- (Rs.17,600 - Rs.5,867 = Rs.11,733/-).

As per the ratio laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, the multiplier to the age of the deceased is 9.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation Ltd., and another reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, total loss of income from the deceased comes to (Rs.11,733/- X 12 X 9 =Rs.12,67,164/-).
Hence, Loss of dependency is determined as Rs.12,67,164/-.

25. Transportation, Funeral expenses, Loss of Estate, Loss of love and affection and Loss of Consortium:- In so far as the funeral and other expenses are concerned, as per the version of the petitioners they have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
But they have not produced any documents to substantiate the said version.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti and other the Compensation under the heads of transportation, funeral expenses, loss of estate, loss of love and affection and loss of consortium has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranaya Sheti
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, that the dependents would be entitled for the transportation of dead body to an extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e.,
(15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Further, for funeral expenses of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/-
i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).

6 Like wise for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.16,500/- i.e., (15,000 X 10/100 =Rs.1,500/- + Rs.15,000/-).
Similarly, for loss of love and affection to the extent of Rs.25,000/- with an enhancement at the rate of 10% every three years.
Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under this head to the tune of Rs.27,500/- i.e., (25,000 X 10/100 =Rs.2,500/- + Rs.25,000/-).
Loss of consortium: it is pertinent to note that, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi case has directed to award an amount of Rs.40,000/- towards consortium.

Subsequently, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 has held that, the term "consortium" is compendious of spousal, parental and filial consortium and directed to award amount in all three categories.

Hence,
in view of the said decisions this tribunal awards under the head of consortium as follows;
(I) Towards spousal consortium: the petitioner No.1 wife is entitled for an amount of Rs.40,000/-
with an enhancement at the ration of 10% in every three years.
Hence, petitioner No.1 is entitled for compensation of Rs.44,000/- (40,000 X 10/100 =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40,000/-).
(ii) Towards filial consortium: Petitioner No.2 is mother of the deceased Prasada.K.S and has lost love and affection of his son and hence, she is entitled for =Rs.4,000/- + Rs.40000/-).
Hence, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads.

Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation award amount of Rs.14,32,164/- which is just and proper.

Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, respondent is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,

ISSUE NO.4:-
27.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.14,32,164/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,. from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for the compensation at the ratio of 80:20.
The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.

Out of awarded amount of petitioner No.1, 80% shall be released to petitioner No.1 on her proper identification and remaining 20% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in her name in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of one year.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner No.2, it is ordered to release the entire amount in their favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
